cues.zh: 视觉上也很流畅。你把东西延迟得足够多，收到输入时就不会卡顿。不用回退。不会让任何人的姿态出现异常。在线和离线玩起来看起来一模一样。

cues.en: It is performant because you don't have to perform rollbacks. We had massive CPU overhead when we were performing lockstep networking.
cues.zh: 性能也好，因为不用执行回滚。我们做锁步网络时CPU开销巨大。

cues.en: That's a very good thing. If you're not latency sensitive,
cues.zh: 这是好事。如果你对延迟不敏感，

cues.en: lockstep is great.
cues.zh: 锁步很棒。

cues.en: Robust.
cues.zh: 很稳健。

cues.en: They're both robust,
cues.zh: 两者都很稳健，

cues.en: which seems a little silly to show you on the slide here. But our experience in the past with peer to peer dead reckoning solutions was that they weren't wildly robust.
cues.zh: 在幻灯片上展示这个似乎有点傻。但我们过去用点对点航位推测方案的经验是，它们并没有特别稳健。

cues.en: They were... Like, it was just constant whack a mole fixing problems. So once you've matured your rollback system and your whole engine is
cues.zh: 它们……就像，一直在打地鼠式地修问题。所以一旦你的回滚系统成熟了，整个引擎都

cues.en: converted over, it's a very robust solution, same as lockstep. Low bandwidth, they're both sending only pad data. You don't have to worry about sending game state, so that's fantastic.
cues.zh: 转换过来，它就是非常稳健的方案，和锁步一样。带宽低，两者都只发手柄数据。不用操心发送游戏状态，这太棒了。

cues.en: Lockstep is not responsive at all. Rollback is responsive. It's the whole reason we switched.
cues.zh: 锁步完全没响应性。回滚有响应性。这正是我们切换的原因。

cues.en: And this last line is
cues.zh: 最后这一行

cues.en: not self explanatory.
cues.zh: 并不那么显而易见。

cues.en: Single frame latency.
cues.zh: 单帧延迟。

cues.en: What this means is when we were in the lockstep approach, I said that your dynamic input latency could vary between five and twenty frames.
cues.zh: 意思是，在之前的锁步（lockstep）方案中，我说过动态输入延迟可能在 5 到 20 帧之间波动。

cues.en: If we waited for one of your frames to
cues.zh: 如果我们非要等你的某一帧

cues.en: bog over the network or be delivered late, we would have to pause the game. In order to not do that, we would keep an eye on your RTT over the past several seconds, and we would change the amount of input latency we were experiencing.
cues.zh: 在网络上堵塞或延迟送达，就不得不暂停游戏。为了避免这种情况，我们会监测过去几秒内的 RTT，并据此调整当前的输入延迟。

cues.en: So you would basically rubber band your input latency over the course of a fight, which meant that a spike in your latency would actually persist for quite a while impacting your input. That's not the case with rollbacks.
cues.zh: 所以在整场战斗中，你的输入延迟基本会忽大忽小，这意味着偶发的网络尖刺会持续影响你的输入很长一段时间。但回滚机制（rollback）就完全不是这样。

cues.en: On every... For every packet sent, that is the only latency that matters. You will essentially... Like, if you did spike for one frame, drop enough packets that you
cues.zh: 对每个……对发出的每个数据包来说，只有它自己的延迟才是关键。实际上……比如哪怕某一帧出现尖刺，丢包丢到

cues.en: bogged,
cues.zh: 卡住了，

cues.en: you would immediately recover assuming the packets started coming in again. Alright. Very relevant for wireless connections.
cues.zh: 只要数据包重新恢复接收，你就能立刻恢复正常。好的，这在无线连接下尤为重要。

cues.en: What do we do first when we bit this thing off?
cues.zh: 当我们刚开始啃这块硬骨头时，第一步是怎么做的？

cues.en: The first goal was to get an idle character rolling back, just two guys standing on a fight line doing nothing.
cues.zh: 第一个目标是让待机角色实现回滚，也就是两个人站在对决线上什么都不做。

cues.en: We turned off almost everything, even essential things that we would have to use for shipping. We would turn off physics and IK and particles and the entirety of online,
cues.zh: 我们几乎关掉了所有东西，甚至是上线发布必需的功能。我们关掉了物理、IK、粒子效果，以及整个联机模块，

cues.en: actually, which sounds kind of nuts. But we wanted to make it work locally before we hooked it up online.
cues.zh: 没错，这听起来有点不可思议。但在联网之前，我们想先让它在本地跑通。

cues.en: So we started doing serialization because we knew that was going to be, you know, the tent pole of this. Basically, you have to save every single frame, and you have to be able to restore to those frames in order to roll back.
cues.zh: 所以我们开始做序列化，因为我们知道这会是整个方案的核心。基本上，每一帧都得保存下来，而且必须能恢复到那些帧，才能回滚。

cues.en: And we had a debug mode called set rollback frames.
cues.zh: 我们有一种叫作“设置回滚帧数”的调试模式。

cues.en: I say seven because that was our decided
cues.zh: 我说七帧，是因为我们决定支持

cues.en: number of rollback frames we would support.
cues.zh: 七帧回滚。

cues.en: I guess as a point of clarity, I keep saying seven. Earlier, I said we support 10 frames of latency. That's the three frames of static input latency plus the seven frames of rollback,
cues.zh: 澄清一下，我一直在说七帧。之前我说过，我们支持 10 帧延迟：其中三帧是固定输入延迟，另外七帧是回滚帧数，

cues.en: which gets us the total of 10 frames.
cues.zh: 加起来总共就是 10 帧。

cues.en: So this rollback... Set rollback frame debug mode was something that we ran with constantly. Everybody did it. It was it was like the number one debug mode that we use from day one all the way till today. We still use it.
cues.zh: 所以这个回滚……“设置回滚帧数”的调试模式，是我们一直在用的。所有人都会用。从第一天起，它就是我们用得最多的调试模式，一直到现在。我们还在用。

cues.en: I... I'm sorry. I really don't think I explained really what was going on there. The set rollback frame seven is every single frame of the game will roll back seven frames and simulate forward.
cues.zh: 我……抱歉，我觉得刚才没把情况解释清楚。“设置回滚帧数为七”，意思是游戏的每一帧都会回滚七帧，再向前模拟。

cues.en: In the case of no divergence or no remote input from your opponent,
cues.zh: 如果没有分歧，也没有收到对手的远程输入，

cues.en: visually, this does nothing. Like, it looks like nothing has happened even though you rewound seven frames and play them all back forward.
cues.zh: 从视觉上看，什么都没发生。也就是说，尽管你回退了七帧，又把它们重新播放了一遍，但看起来毫无变化。

cues.en: So that's how you knew it was working was nothing was happening, and that was success.
cues.zh: 所以，判断它是否正常工作的方法就是看有没有发生变化；什么都没发生，就说明成功了。

cues.en: So a quick breakdown of the tick timeline. This is a diagram I'll use later in the talk.
cues.zh: 下面快速讲一下 tick 的时间线。接下来我还会用到这张图。

cues.en: All I really want to call out here is we service our input and our online, like, the network stuff right up at the front of the frame. It's basically a fixed cost.
cues.zh: 我在这里主要想强调的是，我们把输入和在线部分，也就是网络相关的东西，放在帧的最前端。这基本上是一项固定开销。

cues.en: A restore is restored to previous state. It's one of the first things we do in the frame in the event that you've detected that you have to roll back. The simulated frames are the ones that you simulate forward
cues.zh: 恢复是指恢复到之前的状态。这是我们在帧里最先做的事情之一，前提是你检测到需要回滚。模拟帧则是向前模拟的帧

cues.en: with a stripped down version of the game to get back to the current tick, and then we perform the real render at the end, the full tick with all procedural systems and non gameplay affecting things. This is all one tick. Right? If we're doing our job right, this takes sixteen point six six milliseconds and no more.
cues.zh: 用精简版的游戏逻辑追回到当前 tick，然后在最后执行真正的渲染，也就是完整的 tick，包含所有程序化系统和不影响 gameplay 的东西。这全都在一个 tick 内完成。对吧？如果我们做得好，这应该只花 16.66 毫秒，不能再多。

cues.en: So one of the things that I talked about was that we did serialization first.
cues.zh: 我提到过的一件事是，我们先做了序列化。

cues.en: Serialization
cues.zh: 序列化

cues.en: is a tent pole of this. I'm not gonna talk about it a ton, but here's some.
cues.zh: 是这一切的支柱。我不打算细讲，但这里有一些内容。

cues.en: It's the rollback framework. It was a ring buffer size to the rollback window, meaning it's a ring buffer with one entry per frame.
cues.zh: 这就是回滚框架。它是一个环形缓冲区，大小对应回滚窗口，也就是说每帧一个条目的环形缓冲区。

cues.en: We support seven frames, so it's a seven entry roll... Ring buffer.
cues.zh: 我们支持七帧，所以是一个七条目的环形……环形缓冲区。

cues.en: There's an object serialization interface. You can see it down in the bottom right. It's probably a little bit small.
cues.zh: 有一个对象序列化接口。你能在右下角看到它，可能有点小。

cues.en: Just a basic virtual interface for some of the various edges that we have during serialization,
cues.zh: 就是一个基础的虚接口，对应序列化过程中各种边界情况，

cues.en: saving, and restoration.
cues.zh: 保存和恢复。

cues.en: There will be entries for object creation and destruction. This is a huge problem. If you go the rollback route, you have to handle rolling back to before an object was created and rolling back across the destruction edge as well.
cues.zh: 会有对象创建和销毁的条目。这是个大问题。如果走回滚路线，你必须处理回滚到对象创建之前，以及跨越销毁边界回滚的情况。

cues.en: Done naively, this is going to create and destroy objects all the time.
cues.zh: 如果简单粗暴地做，这会不断创建和销毁对象。

cues.en: We only save mutable data. If something doesn't change, don't save it if at all possible, And it is not delta based, although maybe it should be.
cues.zh: 我们只保存可变数据。如果某些东西不会变，就尽可能不要保存它，而且它不是基于增量的，不过也许本应如此。

cues.en: Restoration is the opposite edge. This is when we have to roll back and restore to previous state. We did this in parallel.
cues.zh: 恢复是相反的那一端。这时我们必须回滚并恢复到之前的状态。我们并行做了这件事。

cues.en: Don't use shared pointer. Shared ownership for serialization purposes
cues.zh: 不要用 shared pointer。为了序列化而使用共享所有权

cues.en: is really bad. Basically, you would have to have two concepts of ownership, both the shared ownership, but then a singular owner
cues.zh: 这会非常糟糕。基本上，你得有两个所有权概念：既是共享所有权，又得有一个单一所有者

cues.en: that is in charge of serialization.
cues.zh: 由这个所有者负责序列化。

cues.en: So we moved away from that. We just heavily moved towards using unique pointer for that sort of thing.
cues.zh: 所以我们不再那样做。我们大量转向使用 unique pointer 来处理这类事情。

cues.en: The serialization restore edge was a simple load balancing and priority scheme. It's a large perf win compared to the single threaded version. So at the very start of this approach,
cues.zh: 序列化恢复这一环节采用简单的负载均衡和优先级方案。与单线程版本相比，这是很大的性能收益。所以在这套方法刚开始时，

cues.en: we were simply doing single threaded restoration,
cues.zh: 我们只是做单线程恢复，

cues.en: and it was it was a small amount of work because we didn't know the full set of everything that we needed to restore, and it took about one point three milliseconds.
cues.zh: 而且当时工作量很小，因为我们还不知道需要恢复的完整内容集合；它大约耗时 1.3 毫秒。

cues.en: At the end of it I'm sorry, two point seven. After we parallelized everything,
cues.zh: 最后，抱歉，是 2.7 毫秒。在我们把所有东西并行化之后，

cues.en: it went down to one point three milliseconds, and that was for twice as much data.
cues.zh: 降到了 1.3 毫秒，而且处理的还是两倍的数据。

cues.en: Also, a point of note, waking threads is slow.
cues.zh: 另外，值得注意的一点是，唤醒线程很慢。

cues.en: We're using condition variables. We found that to be slow largely on both platforms.
cues.zh: 我们用的是条件变量。我们发现它在两个平台上都相当慢。

cues.en: That's something that we'll look into in the future, maybe keeping threads warm, maybe using simple spin locks. It's a very small amount of performance that we're losing there.
cues.zh: 这是我们未来会研究的东西，可能会保持线程热着，也许用简单的自旋锁。我们在那里损失的性能非常小。

cues.en: We also have single threaded post serialization fix up. So after you've done the
cues.zh: 我们还有单线程的后期序列化修复。所以在你完成

cues.en: relatively naive or simple
cues.zh: 相对朴素或简单的

cues.en: serialization restore work, we would do a virtual pass over to link up various pointers and systems that weren't amenable to being serialized.
cues.zh: 序列化恢复工作之后，我们会做一次虚拟遍历，把各种不适合被序列化的指针和系统连接起来。

cues.en: Maybe that's because
cues.zh: 也许是因为

cues.en: it was an asymmetric serialization relationship where you would serialize the object, but you'd have other systems that you really didn't wanna pay serialization costs for. So you would... You'd need to hook those guys back up.
cues.zh: 这是一种不对称的序列化关系，你会序列化对象，但还有其他系统你根本不想承担序列化成本。所以你会……你需要把那些家伙重新接上。

cues.en: Yeah. Bulk serialization and immutable data are hugely preferred. Yeah. Mem copy all your stuff
cues.zh: 对。批量序列化和不可变数据是大大首选。对。直接内存拷贝你所有的东西

cues.en: or
cues.zh: 或者

cues.en: don't change it and, therefore, don't have to serialize it.
cues.zh: 不去改动它，因此就不必序列化它。

cues.en: I'm not gonna read all of this. It's object lifetime. The slides are here if you guys wanna pull down the deck after the fact.
cues.zh: 我不会把这一整页都读了。这是对象生命周期。如果你们想事后下载这份幻灯片，讲义就在这里。

cues.en: Deferred deletion and delete and recreate. You have two choices for your objects,
cues.zh: 延迟删除和删除再重建。对于你的对象，你有两个选择，

cues.en: object lifetime management.
cues.zh: 对象生命周期管理。

cues.en: If you do deferred deletion, you don't really have to handle the creation and destruction of every object every time they die and you roll back across that boundary.
cues.zh: 如果你做延迟删除，你其实不必在每次对象死亡、你回滚跨越那个边界时都处理每个对象的创建和销毁。

cues.en: Delete and recreate is what you get out of the box naively.
cues.zh: 删除再重建是你天真地开箱即得的东西。

cues.en: It's... You'll just constantly delete and recreate your objects, which maybe I'm making that sound bad. Like, sometimes the basic approach is exactly what you need.
cues.zh: 它……你会不断地删除再重建你的对象，也许我把它说得听起来很糟。像是，有时候基本方法正是你需要的。

cues.en: Recreatables.
cues.zh: 可重建对象。

cues.en: This is another thing we did to avoid creating objects all the time.
cues.zh: 这是我们为避免不断创建对象而做的另一件事。

cues.en: The gist of it was you would hash that object.
cues.zh: 其核心思路是对该对象做哈希。

cues.en: And every time you rolled back and played through the creation edge again, you would check the hash of essentially the situation you were in. And if it was the same, you would reuse that object.
cues.zh: 每次回滚并再次播放创建边界时，都会检查所处情境的哈希值。如果相同，就复用那个对象。

cues.en: This is great for sounds and particles.
cues.zh: 这对音效和粒子非常有效。

cues.en: They can be nondeterministic,
cues.zh: 它们可能是不确定的，

cues.en: especially for GPU particles.
cues.zh: 尤其是 GPU 粒子。

cues.en: And since they're nondeterministic,
cues.zh: 而且由于它们是不确定的，

cues.en: if we were to destroy, recreate, and resimulate these guys, we would likely end up with a different result.
cues.zh: 如果我们销毁、重建并重新模拟这些对象，很可能会得到不同的结果。

cues.en: What this would mean is this would be chronic,
cues.zh: 这意味着会出现持续性的问题，

cues.en: like visual popping,
cues.zh: 比如视觉上的跳变，

cues.en: debatably audio popping if you're doing anything dynamic there as well.
cues.zh: 如果你在那里也做了动态处理，还可能有音频跳变。

cues.en: Recreatables,
cues.zh: 可重建对象，

cues.en: it's a relatively simple thing, but the concept was very powerful. Just the ability to hash an object and say, this is the exact same guy. Don't remake it. Don't resimulate it. We saved a lot of performance this way.
cues.zh: 它本身相对简单，但这个概念非常强大。仅仅能够对一个对象做哈希并判断“这就是同一个对象，不要重建它，不要重新模拟它”，就帮我们节省了大量性能。

cues.en: What about gameplay script? We have a proprietary script system called MKScript.
cues.zh: 那玩法脚本呢？我们有一个专有的脚本系统，叫 MKScript。

cues.en: It's c like. This is what our designers work in.
cues.zh: 它类似 C 语言。我们的设计师就用它来工作。

cues.en: We did have to support fiber stack unwinding,
cues.zh: 我们确实必须支持纤程栈展开、

cues.en: fiber stack serialization,
cues.zh: 纤程栈序列化，

cues.en: and objects on the stack that contain dynamic allocations were a pain.
cues.zh: 而栈上含有动态分配的对象则很麻烦。

cues.en: We wrapped them up in a type. We registered them. We cleaned them up separately because the stack was just getting zeroed out.
cues.zh: 我们把它们包装成一个类型，注册它们，并单独清理它们，因为栈只是被清零了。

cues.en: Rollback artifacts.
cues.zh: 回滚产生的画面异常。

cues.en: This is one of the downsides of rollback networking. You will pop your visuals if the divergence is large.
cues.zh: 这是回滚网络模式的缺点之一。如果偏差很大，画面就会出现跳变。

cues.en: Divergence is usually minor. In fact, divergence usually causes no visual artifacts at all. Most of the time when you're receiving remote input from somebody, it doesn't actually affect your game.
cues.zh: 偏差通常很小。事实上，偏差通常根本不会造成任何画面异常。大多数时候，你收到别人的远程输入，其实并不会影响你的游戏。

cues.en: We treat all input as significant,
cues.zh: 我们把所有输入都视为重要输入，

cues.en: and we will roll back every time we get data from the remote player. You may not have to. If you have a
cues.zh: 所以每次收到远程玩家的数据都会回滚。但你不一定非得这么做。如果你有一个

cues.en: more well guarded input system that knows whether input is valid and
cues.zh: 保护得更完善的输入系统，能判断输入是否有效、

cues.en: gameplay affecting,
cues.zh: 是否影响玩法，

cues.en: then you may not have to roll back all the time. But since we need to support divergence and roll back every single frame of the game,
cues.zh: 那你可能就不必每次都回滚。但既然我们需要支持偏差，并且要回滚游戏的每一帧，

cues.en: it doesn't really save us that much.
cues.zh: 那这么做其实也省不了多少。

cues.en: Some low level lessons learned.

cues.en: Limit your mutable state.

cues.en: Handles over pointers wherever performance allows. Handles are inherently a double bounce usually. It depends on your implementation, but they cost extra performance. But what they can allow you to do more easily than a pointer is,
cues.zh: 在性能允许的情况下，优先使用句柄而非指针。句柄本质上通常是双重跳转。这取决于你的实现，但它们会带来额外的性能开销。不过，相比指针，它们能让你更容易做到的是，

cues.en: basically,
cues.zh: 基本上，

cues.en: if you're using a handle,
cues.zh: 如果你使用的是句柄，

cues.en: when it comes time to fix something up post serialization,
cues.zh: 当需要在序列化之后修复某些东西时，

cues.en: you basically don't have to.
cues.zh: 你基本上不需要做任何事。

cues.en: Also, they can allow asymmetric rollback relationships where you have an object that you're referencing via a handle and your system is not serialized, but the object is or vice versa. With a raw pointer, that's much harder to do. You end up having to have these strange post fix up calls where you go and fix up all the pointers in the whole wide world.
cues.zh: 此外，它们还能允许非对称的回滚关系，即你通过句柄引用的对象所在的系统未序列化，但对象本身已序列化，或者反过来。使用原始指针，这要难得多。你最终不得不使用那些奇怪的事后修复调用，去修复整个世界里所有的指针。

cues.en: Avoid shared ownerships of mutable resources. Again, this is what I talked about very early on. Shared ownership, you would end up having to inject another concept of serialization
cues.zh: 避免可变资源的共享所有权。再次强调，这是我很早之前讲过的。共享所有权，你最终不得不注入另一个序列化

cues.en: ownership,
cues.zh: 所有权的概念，

cues.en: which is super dirty and to be avoided.
cues.zh: 这非常肮脏，应当避免。

cues.en: Avoid work in your constructors or destructors. Again, if you're preserving object lifetimes across these
cues.zh: 避免在构造函数或析构函数中做工作。同样，如果你要跨越这些

cues.en: creation and destruction boundaries, you can't trust your constructors and destructors to trigger when they normally would.
cues.zh: 创建和销毁边界来保持对象生命周期，你就不能信任构造函数和析构函数会在它们通常该触发的时候触发。

cues.en: Lean on MEM copies and buffer swaps instead of dynamic fix up. Yep. Yep. Do that.

cues.en: This is a huge one. This is a big deal. This feels like, of course, this is the way it should work. Design your game systems to drive visual state, not depend on it. We have a whole bunch of code that says, tell me where my right hand is. Oh, where is the head? And it does all of these things. And it's literally saying, tell me where the joint is. But if you stop running your procedural systems, those answers are all wrong. So we end up having to cut a whole bunch of corners to make all of those answers right. And if we had done a cleaner job upfront of segregating these two systems, we'd be much better off.
cues.zh: 这非常关键。这是一件大事。感觉上，这当然就是它应有的工作方式。设计游戏系统时，应该由其来驱动视觉状态，而不是依赖视觉状态。我们有一大堆代码，比如：告诉我我的右手在哪。哦，头部在哪？它做了所有这些事情。它字面意思就是在问，告诉我关节在哪里。但如果你停止运行你的程序化系统，这些答案就全错了。所以我们最终不得不走各种捷径，来让所有这些答案变正确。如果我们一开始能把这两个系统隔离开来，做得更干净一些，情况就会好得多。

cues.en: Design systems to update with variable time steps. It is extremely convenient when you don't have to run something eight times, and you can run it at intermediate points and still get effectively the same result.
cues.zh: 设计系统时支持可变时间步长更新。当你不需要运行某东西八次，而只需在中间点运行它却依然能得到实际上相同的效果时，这会极其方便。

cues.en: If you can update parametrically, that's even better because you probably only need to update once.
cues.zh: 如果你能进行参数化更新，那就更好了，因为你可能只需要更新一次。

cues.en: Everyone should work with debug rollback systems enabled. It's the fastest way to find things that go wrong. cues.zh: 每个人都应该在开启调试回溯系统的情况下工作。这是发现问题最快的方法。当你的策划在没有开启调试系统的情况下工作时，他们会觉得自己制作的东西完全没问题，直到后来——你知道的，因为QA碰巧发现了Bug。

cues.en: I don't have to actually roll something back if I don't respond to it until I'm guaranteed for it to have actually occurred.
